questions.stem:
A circle $C$ has equation
$x^2 + y^2 + 4x - 10y - 21 = 0$
Find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) (i) the coordinates of the centre of $C$,
(ii) the exact value of the radius of $C$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Attempts $(x\pm 2)^2 + (y\pm 5)^2 \ldots = 0$ (attempts to complete the square on both terms or states the centre as $(\pm 2, \pm 5)$).
(i) A1: Centre $(-2, 5)$. Allow $x=-2, y=5$. This alone can score both marks even following incorrect lines e.g. $(x+2)^2 \ldots (y-5)^2 \ldots = \ldots$ where $\ldots$ could be a minus sign or blank.
(ii) B1: Radius $\sqrt{50}$ or $5\sqrt{2}$. You may isw after a correct answer. If a candidate attempts to use $x^2+y^2+2fx+2gy+c=0$ then M1 may be awarded for a centre of $(\pm 2, \pm 5)$.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The point $P(5, 4)$ lies on $C$.
(b) Find the equation of the tangent to $C$ at $P$, writing your answer in the form $y = mx + c$, where $m$ and $c$ are constants to be found.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) B1ft: Gradient of radius $= \dfrac{(5)-4}{(-2)-5} = -\dfrac{1}{7}$ which needs to be in simplest form. Correct answer for the gradient of the line joining $P(5,4)$ to their centre. You may ft on their centre but the value must be fully simplified.
M1: Uses $m_2 = -\dfrac{1}{m_1}$ to find gradient of tangent. Awarded for using $m_2=-\dfrac{1}{m_1}$ to find gradient of tangent.

Condone bracketing slips only. If the candidate uses the form $y=mx+c$ they must use $x$ and $y$ the correct way around and proceed as far as $c=\ldots$
A1: $y = 7x - 31$ stated. It must be written in this form. (It cannot be awarded from $y=mx+c$ by just stating $c=-31$.)

$P = 12x - x^{\frac{3}{2}} - 120$
where $P$ is the annual profit measured in thousands of pounds and $\pounds x$ is the selling price of the watch.

Don't be too concerned with the mechanics of process. Condone an attempted solution of $\frac{dP}{dx}\ldots 0$ where $\ldots$ could be an inequality.

questions.stem:
Figure 1 shows a sketch of part of the curve $C$ with equation $y=\mathrm{f}(x)$ where
$\mathrm{f}(x) = \dfrac{36}{x^2} + 2x - 13 \qquad x > 0$
Using calculus,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find the range of values of $x$ for which $\mathrm{f}(x)$ is increasing,
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1A1: $\left(\mathrm{f}'(x)\right) = -\dfrac{72}{x^3} + 2$. M1: Attempts $\mathrm{f}'(x)$ with one index correct. Allow for $x^{-2}\to x^{-3}$ or $2x\to 2$. A1: $\mathrm{f}'(x)=-\frac{72}{x^3}+2$ correct but may be unsimplified $\mathrm{f}'(x)=36\times-2x^{-3}+2$.
dM1: Attempts to solve $\mathrm{f}'(x)=0\Rightarrow x=\ldots$ via $x^{\pm n}=k$, $k>0$. Attempts to find where $\mathrm{f}'(x)=0$. Score for $x^n=k$ where $k>0$ and $n\neq\pm1$ leading to $x=\ldots$. Do not allow this to be scored from an equation that is adapted incorrectly to get a positive k. Allow this to be scored from an attempt at solving $\mathrm{f}'(x)\ldots0$ where $\ldots$ can be any inequality.
A1: $x > \sqrt[3]{36}$ oe. Achieves $x>\sqrt[3]{36}$ or $x>6^{\frac{2}{3}}$. Allow $x\geqslant\sqrt[3]{36}$ or $x\geqslant 6^{\frac{2}{3}}$ but not $x>\left(\frac{1}{36}\right)^{-\frac{1}{3}}$. We require an exact value but remember to isw. An answer of 3.302 usually implies the first 3 marks.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) show that $\displaystyle\int_{2}^{9}\left(\dfrac{36}{x^2} + 2x - 13\right)\mathrm{d}x = 0$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1A1: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{36}{x^2}+2x-13\,\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{36}{x}+x^2-13x\ (+c)$. M1: For $x^n\to x^{n+1}$ seen on either $\frac{36}{x^2}$ or $2x$. Indices must be processed. eg $x^{1+1}\to x^2$. A1: $\int\frac{36}{x^2}+2x-13\,dx = -\frac{36}{x}+x^2-13x$ which may be unsimplified. Eg $x^2\leftrightarrow\frac{2x^2}{2}$. Allow with $+c$.
dM1A1*: Uses limits 9 and 2 $= \left(-\dfrac{36}{9}+9^2-13\times9\right)-\left(-\dfrac{36}{2}+2^2-13\times2\right)=0$ *. dM1: Substitutes 9 and 2 into their integral and subtracts either way around. Condone missing brackets. Dependent upon the previous M. A1*: Completely correct integration with either embedded values seen or calculated values $(-40)-(-40)$. Note that this is a given answer and so the bracketing must be correct.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The point $P(2,0)$ and the point $Q(6,0)$ lie on $C$.
Given $\displaystyle\int_{2}^{6}\left(\dfrac{36}{x^2}+2x-13\right)\mathrm{d}x = -8$
(c) (i) state the value of $\displaystyle\int_{6}^{9}\left(\dfrac{36}{x^2}+2x-13\right)\mathrm{d}x$
(ii) find the value of the constant $k$ such that $\displaystyle\int_{2}^{6}\left(\dfrac{36}{x^2}+2x+k\right)\mathrm{d}x = 0$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c)(i) B1: 8. For sight of 8. Allow this to be scored from a restart, from a calculator or $\ldots = 8$.
(c)(ii) M1: This may be awarded in a variety of ways: A restart, for this to be awarded all terms must be integrated with $k\to kx$, the limits 6 and 2 applied, the linear expression in k must be set equal to 0 and a solution attempted. An attempt at solving $\int_2^6 k+13\,dx=8$ or equivalent, looking for the linear equation $-8+4(13+k)=0$ or $4(13+k)=8$ and a solution attempted. Recognising that the curve needs to be moved up 2 units. Sight of $\frac{8}{6-2}$ or $-13+2$.
A1: $k=-11$. This alone can be awarded both marks as long as no incorrect working is seen.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $\int_2^6\left(\frac{36}{x^2}+2x+k\right)dx=0\Rightarrow\left[-\frac{36}{x}+x^2+kx\right]_2^6=0\Rightarrow(30+6k)-(-14+2k)=0$ $44+4k=0\Rightarrow k=-11$ M1 A1
